A `UnitOccurrence` identifies one source version and a locator: PDF physical
page plus printed page and bounding region where available; HTML element or
XBRL fact/context identifiers; text line/character span in a pinned extraction.
Locators retain table headings, footnotes and continuation links needed for
meaning. A text locator alone does not establish faithful PDF extraction.
Units identify parent section, annual/quarterly/semiannual package root, and
disposition. An occurrence is never deleted because another occurrence has the
same text. Byte-identical span content may share a content ID; semantic
equivalence additionally requires compatible context and an explicit review.

A `ReportedAssertion` links every supporting occurrence and preserves literal
text/value. An `ExtractionReading` identifies a candidate reading and its
review events. An `Interpretation` identifies the exact extraction versions,
financial scope, dependencies, modality and proposed meaning. A `Derivation`
records input versions, expression, result context and assumptions. An
`Assumption` has an author, rationale, scope and alternatives and cannot be
labelled issuer evidence. A `Conflict` links incompatible candidates and their
affected queries; conflicting faithful readings both survive.

The reviewed-assertion population counts identified assertion candidates at a
named layer, once per contextual assertion identity. It reports accepted,
rejected, pending and unresolved counts and aliases explicitly. It also retains
unread/unstructured source units, whose unknown assertion count cannot be
treated as zero. A denominator of six discovered candidates means six candidates
reviewed to some disposition, not six assertions in the whole real report.

## Identity, corrections and duplicate information

The immutable occurrence key is `(source_version, locator, occurrence_id)`.
This is different from a content-body hash or a contextual assertion identity.
Financial context includes legal entity, perimeter/version, concept/mapping
version, dimensions, calendar/version, reporting interval/instant, currency,
unit/scale, sign convention, measurement basis, source vintage and reported
precision/rounding support. The definitive portable encoding remains an IR and
persistence obligation; these components are the semantic requirements.

Context equality is necessary but not sufficient for merging assertions. An
explicit alias/equivalence decision must also establish the same assertion and
compatible source/reading lineage. Source occurrences stay distinct after such
a decision. Overlapping rounding intervals, equal displayed numbers, common
labels or a matching period never independently establish equivalence.
Source restatement and extraction correction remain different change kinds.
A corrected entity, unit or period can create a new reading even when the number
does not change. The new reading names the superseded version, supporting source
and reason; it does not modify original bytes or automatically resolve an issuer
conflict. Duplicate evidence must not later become independent likelihood input.

In fixture X01, a parent-only historical-cost reading and a consolidated
fair-value reading both display 100 for the same concept/year/currency. They
remain two assertions with separate occurrences. X02 links two faithful
occurrences of one supported assertion without creating two independent facts.

New record digests use `SHA256(UTF8("accdsl.portable.v1/" + schema) || 0x00 ||
canonical(record))`. Canonical JSON is UTF-8, sorted ASCII object keys, no
insignificant whitespace and no floats, NaN, infinity, duplicate keys or invalid
Unicode scalar values. Strings retain their decoded code points; JSON escapes
and literal Unicode for the same code point are equivalent. Composed and
decomposed Unicode are distinct unless a named transformation explicitly maps
them. Identifiers are ASCII; financial labels and quoted source text may be
Unicode. This deliberately replaces implicit global NFC normalization in the
exploratory Core 0 proposal: source spelling must not be silently changed.
Raw source identity always hashes original bytes, outside this record encoding.

Array order is meaningful except for schema-declared sets. In this version,
`dependencies`, module declarations by key, context dimensions by axis key, and
the explicit IR `all_of`/`any_of` operand sets are canonical sets; reject duplicate
keys or members before sorting by canonical UTF-8 bytes. All other arrays,
including event schedules, journal lines, source spans and diagnostic priority
sequences, retain order. Rational reduction and set sorting occur during typed
construction; a purported canonical wire record violating them is rejected.
There is no general algebraic simplification, alias folding or equivalence proof
in hashing. Hash equality supports byte identity under the chosen encoding, not
economic equivalence or source truth.

For byte-level interoperability the serializer emits literal valid non-ASCII
Unicode scalars in UTF-8. Escape only quotation mark, reverse solidus and control
characters U+0000–U+001F: use `\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\f`, `\r` for their five named
controls and lowercase `\u00xx` for the remainder. Do not escape solidus. Integers
use minimal base-ten text, with no leading plus, zeroes or negative zero. Input
escapes are decoded before canonical output. Object keys are ASCII and ordered
by unsigned ASCII bytes. These rules, set normalization and rational reduction
fix one byte string for every valid typed record; arbitrary JSON writer defaults
are not part of the definition.

## I2. Operation signatures and ownership

In this table each listed input is required unless explicitly marked optional.
Lists are explicit even when empty. Domain records retain the detailed fields
in their named contracts; the table does not replace them with untyped prose.

| Versioned operation | Arguments → payload | Effect and controlling contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source.prepare@1` | package manifest, source snapshot, adapter/config lock, prior review, traversal budget and optional continuation → ExtractionPreparation | Acquires/preserves sources and constructs candidates under extraction-v1; no semantic admission |
| `review.propose@1` | target Ref, layer, decision kind, evidence Refs, actor, rationale, replacement Ref or null → ReviewProposal | Candidate construction; accepts no layer |
| `review.commit@1` | ReviewProposal, expected review view/revision → immutable ReviewDecision and new view | Review transaction under evidence E4/persistence P4; admissible action/layer required |
| `time.select@1` | package/view, investor/system/exploratory mode, cutoffs, revision and unknown-time policy → selected assertions, conflicts and temporal obligations | Pure selection under time T1–T6; no invented ingestion or publication time |

## Source, reading and financial meaning

Retain the complete original instance as a BlobRef and SourceVersion before
reading facts. Every fact, context and unit gets its own UnitOccurrence with
half-open byte offsets in those exact bytes and a structural path. An optional
XML ID supplements that locator; it does not replace it. Equal fact values at
different locations remain distinct occurrences and assertion candidates.
Offsets must come from an independently checked lexical source map in a future
adapter. A parsed tree, source line, fragment identifier or reserialization
alone cannot recover original byte offsets. The supplied offsets are authored
for the retained synthetic UTF-8 file, not produced by Arelle.

The documentary input packet is an authored reading of that XML, including
every retained field and raw span. It is not a serialization of an Arelle
session. LegacyImport retains the packet's exact bytes and original ID; the
separate SourceVersion retains the XML bytes. A future native packet needs
its own pinned decoder, upstream validation results and checked lexical map.
The packet's explicit fixture type labels are author assumptions, not inspected
taxonomy declarations. No XSD, DTS or XBRL validation is claimed.

Original tokens, XML-decoded text, proposed numeric values, declaration defaults

the converter has no admission or posting authority.

`profile.json` declares exact body fields and type signatures for SourceVersion,
UnitOccurrence, XbrlContextEvidence, XbrlUnitEvidence, Context,
ReportedAssertion, ConversionMethod, ImportMapping, ImportComparison and
LegacyImport. Every record uses exactly L1's six fields. Each kind has its own
versioned proposed schema; a profile cannot reinterpret a frozen native digest.
All body Ref links occur in dependencies, with no extra dependencies. Required
transitive record closure is finite and acyclic. BlobRefs require separate
exact byte closure. Dependencies and ImportMapping.outputs are canonical sets;
XML measure/dimension order, occurrence lists and mappings retain their order.

Every output body's top-level field has a mapping. source_path is a JSON
Pointer into the retained authored packet; target_path is a JSON Pointer into
the output record. Equal-decoded mappings require exact JSON typed equality;

Schema validity and correspondence are bounded engineering checks. Admission
requires a separate E4 review decision in a requested immutable view; the
input packet, proposed Context and converter cannot grant it. No operation
request, runtime result, accounting entry or external service is implemented by
these files. General native parsing, taxonomy resolution/validation, a checked
lexical map, real-filing translation, full context admission, exact dependency

Selection follows the mission's preservation need: native facts carry contexts,
units and occurrence relationships that a flattened table cannot reconstruct.
The exact earlier API, inline-value and fact-identity inspections remain the
technical support. Use one session in its owning thread per process. Request
validation and validationExitCode, disable formula execution, automatic plugins
and additional packages, copy required records while the model remains open,
then close it. Process isolation may support later parallelism, but no throughput
claim follows. Retain logs and model errors as well as the controller Boolean.

Replay of the same request identity and exact bytes returns the same proposal
receipt; the same identity with changed bytes is a conflict. Cancellation before
completion publishes only the declared partial proposal and unresolved frontier.
No review acceptance, journal authorization, accounting commit or successful
runtime validation is generated by these fixtures. Later product integration
must translate the envelope into existing evidence/review requests and test
that translation against the full portable schemas. Passing documentary field
and arithmetic checks cannot establish that runtime translation.

Use the previously inspected session lifecycle with no optional plugins or additional package groups: request validation and its error-sensitive return, disable formula execution, and copy facts and their contexts before closing the session. Each owning process admits one session at a time. For this particular Apple archive, the recorded map has 27 resources and 3,551 reference edges. Resolving those static references does not establish XBRL validation or closure of every financial note.

The deterministic PDF comparator is the retained pdfplumber source, used for character and page geometry on machine-generated documents. Its output remains a proposal to be checked against the located page. A page that needs unadmitted OCR remains unresolved, with its original bytes and manual inspection route preserved. Docling, TableFormer and OCR are separate candidate paths. They do not become an automatic fallback that silently changes the selected method, model terms or resource budget.

There are three distinct forms of reproducibility here. A source selection identifies the code and technical evidence. A resolved environment identifies the actual platform, Python build, every direct and transitive package version and hash, enabled extras, model and taxonomy bytes, and applicable notices. An executed compatibility check establishes what those installed components actually do together. The present selection establishes the first. Arelle's 15 base requirement ranges and three build requirements remain an inventory; they are not an exact transitive lock. Before runtime, resolve that inventory for the selected platform and inspect the resulting compatibility and terms. Any changed dependency, transformation registry, taxonomy or configuration creates a new identity and invalidates dependent admission.

Offline access is exact URI-to-bytes resolution. An absent file, changed hash, wrong namespace or missing required fragment returns the affected dependency as unresolved before accepting its financial values. A cached pathname is insufficient. Original schemas remain unchanged, and the isolated cache or external resolver may provide only admitted bytes. Substituting a newer taxonomy would change the interpretation problem.

Terms also attach to different things: code, dependencies, issuer documents, taxonomies and model weights. The earlier source-specific dispositions remain binding evidence limits. In particular, an unversioned FASB page displaying 2027 does not establish the terms applicable to a retained 2024 package; the missing component-specific XBRL Software Notice remains a source dependency. Unresolved model-weight terms constrain the corresponding model path. They do not resolve or negate the separate native-XBRL source decision. No distribution or blanket legal clearance follows from this selection.

Eleven complete documentary exchanges test the proposed boundary without executing a converter. Every synthetic source body, context, unit and occurrence span is supplied. Raw ``1,234'' under an admitted grouping transform and scale \(-3\) produces \(1.234\); precision metadata does not scale it again. A nil occurrence remains unknown. Equal values in different contexts stay separate. Unknown transforms, missing contexts or typed-dimension values, absent resources and changed hashes retain unresolved records instead of guessed facts.

A cancelled case retains its completed proposal and unprocessed frontier. Repeating an identical request preserves its proposal receipt; changing bytes under the same identity is a conflict. All results remain proposed or unresolved, and none claims package completeness, review acceptance or an accounting commit. These are authored expected exchanges with independently checked transformations. Their closed documentary envelope is a verification format for the proposal; it does not alter the portable product schemas or establish runtime translation into them. That translation and the exact environment remain prerequisites of the later implementation.

Two evaluations of a variable-set for a given input are identical variable-set evaluations if each fact variable evaluation in one variable set evaluation is identical to the evaluation of the same fact variable in the other variable set evaluation. Two evaluations of a variable-set for a given input are different variable-set evaluations if they are not identical . All variable evaluations begin with evaluation of the XPath expression implied by the variable. An XPath expression has a variable dependency if the expression includes an XPath variable reference. Error code xbrlve:unresolvedDependency MUST be thrown if there an XPath expression to be evaluated has a variable dependency that cannot be resolved to a variable or parameter. 4.1 Binding as a sequence A variable binds as a sequence if it has a @bindAsSequence attribute equal to true . Otherwise, it does not bind as a sequence. The result of a variable evaluation depends upon whether the variable binds as a sequence. For a general variable that does not bind as a sequence, the result of its evaluation is any one of the items in its source sequence . For a general variable that does bind as a sequence, the result of its evaluation is the source sequence. For a fact variable, if the source sequence is not empty and if it does not bind as a sequence, then the result of its evaluation is either its fallback value or any one of the facts in its source sequence .

For a fact variable, if the source sequence is not empty and if it does bind as a sequence, then the result of its evaluation is either its fallback value or any sequence of facts in the source sequence that meets the following conditions: All facts in the evaluation result are also in the source sequence of the fact variable. No fact occurs more than once in the evaluation result. Each uncovered aspect of each fact in the evaluation result sequence MUST have an equivalent aspect value for all of the other facts in the evaluation result. All facts in the evaluation result MUST have the same set of uncovered aspect s. If the @matches attribute on the fact variable is omitted or is equal to false then the evaluation result MUST NOT contain any aspect-matched facts . The evaluation result MUST include all possible facts from the source sequence that meet the previous conditions. The order of the facts in the evaluation result for fact variables is application dependent. Evaluation results that only differ with regard to the order of the facts that they contain are deemed to be the same evaluation.

value assertion expression is the XPath expression contained by the @test attribute on a value assertion. 3 The processing model for value assertions The assertion data set for a value assertion is an evaluation of the variable set defined by the value assertion. Each different evaluation of a value assertion's variable set constitutes a different data set for the variable assertion. Value assertion expressions MAY have dependencies on any of the variables and parameters in the variable sets defined by their value assertions. For this reason, value assertions can only be evaluated if the variable set that constitutes their data set has also been evaluated. Value assertion expressions are evaluated using the <xbrli:xbrl> element of the input XBRL instance as the context item . The variables and parameters in the data set are in scope for the evaluation of the value assertion expression. A value assertion test is the effective Boolean value produced by evaluating the value assertion expression given a suitable data set. Appendix A Normative schema

3 The processing model for all assertions This section defines key features of the processing model for all assertions . Assertion specifications may augment these key features of the processing model. All assertions are tested against an assertion input. An assertion input , is a input XBRL instance and the values of the parameters supplied with that input XBRL instance . An assertion data set is a subset of information in or derived from the assertion input that can be tested against an assertion. An assertion evaluation is the result produced by testing an assertion against an assertion data set An assertion input can contain more than one assertion data set for a given assertion. Given an assertion input , an assertion MAY be evaluated once for each assertion data set in the assertion input. An assertion test is the effective Boolean value produced by an assertion evaluation. An assertion evaluation is satisfied when its assertion test equals true . An assertion evaluation is not satisfied when its assertion test equals false . Assertion specifications MUST define the assertion data sets for the assertions being specified. Assertion specifications MUST also specify how the assertions being defined are to be evaluated using the assertion data sets to produce assertion tests.

2.3 Node Identity Each node has a unique identity. Every node in an instance of the data model is unique: identical to itself, and not identical to any other node. ( Atomic values do not have identity; every instance of the value “5” as an integer is identical to every other instance of the value “5” as an integer.) Note: The concept of node identity should not be confused with the concept of a unique ID, which is a unique name assigned to an element by the author to represent references using ID/IDREF correlation.
